text.p: Queensland Cotton Holdings Ltd, Australia's largest ginner and marketer of cotton, said planting of next year's cotton crop was well underway in the best planting conditions in five years.
Major increases in production were expected in New South Wales (NSW) because of available water supply, the company said in its half year report released on Friday.
"All cotton areas in Queensland are facing the best planting conditions for five years, giving us strong optimism in assessing the future of our operations in both states," it said.

Water shortages had eased in the Emerald region of Queensland, giving the region the capacity to achieve 60-70 percent of pre-drought crop levels, Queensland Cotton said. It said the upgrade of its Dalby gin would enable the company to cater for expected increase in volume on the Darling Downs.
Capital expansion over the past few years also would allow the company to benefit from increased production in NSW, the report said.
Forecasts by the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics indicated a record 1997/98 Australian crop of 2.25 million- to three million 500 lb bales, the company noted.
Australia's previous record cotton crop was 2.2 million bales in 1991/92, although ABARE has also forecast a record crop of 2.6 million bales for 1996/97.
